implementation_notes: Ruby has no multiton in the standard library, but Hash plus class-level state makes the idiom short: the class keeps @instances in a class instance variable, the factory memoises with @instances[key] ||= new(key), and private_class_method :new keeps the constructor closed. Under threads the memoisation must run inside a class-level Mutex#synchronize, and the mutex must be created eagerly because lazy @mutex ||= Mutex.new is itself a race; for a concurrent map without hand-written locking, concurrent-ruby's Concurrent::Map is the usual replacement.
pitfalls: @instances and @mutex are class instance variables: a subclass calling the factory sees its own (nil) hash and mutex, so a subclass silently gets a different registry - use a constant or class_variable_set if inheritance must share it.
||= is not atomic: without the mutex two threads both see nil and both call new, and the loser's resources stay open.
Ractors cannot share the hash or the Mutex at all; a Ractor-based program needs a per-Ractor registry or an explicit channel protocol.
